patches.fact: Standard descent route and exit trailhead
patches.find: From the true summit, descend as for the standard south-side line: east ridge toward the false summit, traverse the south face to round it at its easiest point (~9,000'), then down the broad Cascadian Couloir — about 4,600 feet of Class 2-3 scree, talus, and snow — to Ingalls Creek, and back out over Longs Pass to the Esmeralda Basin/Ingalls Creek trailhead. This is a walk-off with no rappelling required on the standard descent; note that this trailhead is not the Mountaineer Creek trailhead used for the approach, so a car shuttle (or a long overland return) is part of planning this route as a car-to-car day.
patches.replace: From the true summit, retrace toward the false summit and descend the Sherpa Glacier, entered just east of where the Ice Cliff Glacier couloir tops out near 8,200 ft, back to the moraine camp; later in the season, once the Sherpa has melted out, parties go around Sherpa Peak to Sherpa Pass instead. Then walk out the Mountaineer Creek climbers' trail to the Stuart Lake trailhead, the same one used for the approach, so no car shuttle is needed. The glacier descent is technical, especially in the dark, so keep the axe, crampons and crevasse kit for it.

A Northwest Forest Pass or America the Beautiful pass is needed to park. This approach is outside the Enchantment Permit Area, so no lottery permit applies; the free self-issued Alpine Lakes Wilderness permit covers day and overnight use.
